acts.d: Attackers conducted reconnaissance by learning about EDRPOU and M.E.Doc, queried EDRPOU website, and changed their computer language sets to the Ukrainian alphabet

Attackers added malicious functionality to the files containing software updates for M.E.Doc to collect a list of all EDRPOUs associated with computers using the M.E.Doc software and had downloaded the update file and to send a cookie back to the Update Server

Attackers added malicious functionality to the files containing software updates for M.E.Doc to collect a list of all EDRPOUs associated with computers using the M.E.Doc software which would eventually deliver the NotPetya
Attackers rerouted internet traffic from computers updating M.E.Doc software via the Update Server to France-based server controlled by attackers
NotPetya drops the ransomware DLL perfc.dat, writes a resource to C:\Windows\dllhost.dat, and drops its ransomware splash and warning files
Malware starts subroutine and hashes every running process on the system and sets PROC_FLAG. It is looking for three hardcoded hashes: Kaspersky, Symantec, Norton Security.
Malware attempts to determine privilege of its running process and sets the PRIV_FLAG: SeTcbPrivilege, SeDebugPrivilege, SeShutdownPrivilege
Operates as a modified version of Mimikatz and uses a named pipe to extract credentials from LSASS
Duplicates another user's token and allows attacker to escalate privileges and impersonate another user to spread the malware
To move laterally, NotPetya tests for vulnerable SMBv1 condition (Eternal Blue/Romance exploit) and deploys an SMB backdoor

NotPetya will not encrypt the MFT and will simply overwrite the first 10 sectors of the physical disk with uninitialized data. It will still render the machine unbootable by overwriting the 2nd section of the C:\, however, there is the possibility to recover MBR.
Malware reads and encodes MBR with a custom boot loader that will encrypt the MFT.
To move laterally, the malware logs into any version of SMB with the stolen tokens or harvested credentials and does a UNC write to Admin$ to execute malware
Malware issues commands to gather list of known IP addresses and TCP endpoints and enumerate domain controllers
To deploy NotPetya on the system, a staging DLL is injected into lsass.exe
NotPetya creates a scheduled task that triggers a reboot 60 min after execution by default
Malware executes either using PsExec or WMIC as rundll32.exe
NotPetya written to c:/windows and executed by the staging DLL as rundll32.exe
System reboots, displays decoy message
The custom boot loader encrypts the MFT. NotPetya also encrypted files with specific extensions.
The malware clears setup, system, security, application, and USN journal logs
The custom boot loader initiates a disk reboot, and the NotPetya ransomware note is displayed
The data is not recoverable
